P1.evidence: The only call in the batch where the frame was never set at all. After small talk the rep asked 'You spoke with Kyla, right?' and 'How was that conversation for you?' — the setter was referenced but nothing was read back, and the prospect had to guess at what had been passed on ('I'm not sure how much of it was recorded or what was written down'). No expectations were set, no agreement was sought, and the open question was never asked; the prospect simply launched into a five-minute self-introduction and the rep let him.

P2.evidence: The back half of the phase ran well and in one clean sweep: 'What's your food like? What kind of stuff are you eating?' with a good weekend follow-up, and 'the last thing I would check would be like your energy levels and your sleep', which produced the erratic-sleep picture and the vitamin D history. Training frequency asked and confirmed. The front half is absent: age, height and weight were all volunteered and none were asked — the rep only reflected the weight back — and there was no health-conditions question and no injury or movement-limitation question anywhere on the call. Occupation volunteered, though the on-your-feet element did emerge ('at work, I am mostly on my feet... it's a big facility, laboratory').

P3.evidence: Two good surface questions and then nothing: 'If we were to fast forward six months, where do you want to be at?' and, when the answer was abstract, the right follow-up — 'What is the lifestyle change you want to make? Like if you picture the lifestyle you want in six months, what's different?' Neither was pushed past the description. No aesthetics or function question, no 'something you can't do right now', no bridge to what is actually driving it at 30, and no reflect-back. P3f is the conspicuous miss: a married man whose wife lives in another country and who travels to family every weekend was never asked who else this impacts, on a call that turned entirely on whether he could commit.

P4.evidence: The phase never ran. Not one question about what he had tried, what happened, or why it did not stick — and this prospect handed over the single most important fact in the call unprompted: his own unstructured approach took him from 92 kg to 84 kg. Whether that will stall, and why, is the entire commercial argument, and it was never touched. The gap was never named, and 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own?' would have been the exact question, since on his own evidence he can.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame of any kind. The two-year question was never asked of a 30-year-old whose stated concern is that work has been steadily displacing his health since 2020, and there was no settle-for question, no 'why not' and no line in the sand.

P6.evidence: A readiness gate was run before presenting anything, which is the phase's intent: 'Most people who come in here... it's more so like I'm ready to change. I'm ready to come. I'm ready to do this. Do you feel like you're there?' Neither scripted question was used — no belief question and no all-in question. And where the script says to return to Phase 5 when hesitation surfaces, the rep instead ended the sale: 'what I think you should do... try and do that yourself.' The gate held, but it was used as an exit rather than as a loop.

P11.evidence: No offer presented and no close attempted; no price was spoken at any point in the call, so no payment or onboarding step was reachable.

objection_plays.detail: The strongest OD trigger in the batch — shifts starting at 4am or ending at 2am, weekly inter-emirate travel, and 'I'm not sure that I'll be able to commit for a long time'. One move ran, the prioritise-and-make-time reframe: 'it comes to a case of prioritizing the time, right? Making the time so that you can get what you want.' None of the rest: no 'things never slow down', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', and critically no 'what if all you had to do was show up and everything else was handled', which is the direct answer to a man whose objection is cognitive load rather than desire.

Script gap, and the sharpest one in this batch. The prospect rejected the playbook's engine outright: 'I'm not committing to a weight, rather, I would like to commit to a lifestyle change... the moment I put a date or a number or something like that, then it becomes a pressure.' Every phase from P3 to P6 is built on goal specificity, consequence and a line in the sand. There is no play for a prospect who has explicitly told you that framing will make him disengage, and no low-commitment on-ramp to offer him — he asked for one directly: 'maybe one 20-minute workout on a kettlebell, maybe one or two days a week, I want to try, be confident... and then based on that, increase it.'

Script gap: no protocol for disqualification. This is the second call in the batch closed out by the rep before the offer was presented or priced. There is no defined test for when to disqualify, no requirement to present before doing so, no nurture mechanism beyond 'follow the Instagram', and no way to distinguish these in reporting from prospects who heard the offer and declined. Two of five sales calls in this batch never saw a price.

notes: Good diet, sleep and energy questioning inside a call with no frame, no past-attempts phase and no consequence frame — then a disqualification made on a readiness answer the rep never tried to move. The coachable moment is at 00:12:16: the prospect said he had lost 8 kg on his own with no plan, and that is either the reason he does not need coaching or the reason he does, and the rep asked nothing about it either way.
